title: The deadliest hunter on Earth looks like a moon lander

hook.narration: The deadliest hunter on Earth is a virus shaped like a moon lander.
fact_sources: suttle + t4: 'deadliest' = most kills per day of any biological entity (framing, supported by the ~20%/day estimate); T4 morphology resembles a lunar lander (head, tail, six fibres)

scenes.narration: It's called a bacteriophage, and it only hunts bacteria.
It lands on one, legs first, and grips the surface.
Then it squats, and punches a needle through the wall.
Its DNA shoots inside, and takes over the cell.
The bacterium stops living, and starts building phages.
fact_sources: t4: host machinery is redirected to phage production

scenes.narration: In half an hour, it is packed with a hundred copies.
fact_sources: t4: ~30 min, ~100-150 per cell (VO says 'a hundred')

scenes.narration: Then they dissolve the wall from inside. Pop.
fact_sources: t4: holin + endolysin lyse the wall from inside

scenes.narration: Every one flies off to find another.
fact_sources: t4: released phages diffuse to new hosts

scenes.narration: In the oceans, viruses kill a fifth of all microbes, every day.
And they can't touch you. Human cells are not on the menu.
The deadliest hunter on Earth is not hunting you.

visual.v1: loop hold: phage descends to its frame-0 pose

sources.suttle: Suttle CA, 'Marine viruses - major players in the global ecosystem', Nat Rev Microbiol 5:801-812 (2007), doi:10.1038/nrmicro1750: viruses kill ~20% of ocean microbial biomass per day (an estimate; varies by system)
sources.t4: Escherichia virus T4 (textbook biology; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escherichia_virus_T4): long tail fibres attach, baseplate seats, contractile sheath drives the tail tube through the envelope, DNA enters; lytic cycle ~30 min at 37 C; burst ~100-150 phages; lysis needs holin + endolysin (PMC93561)
sources.host: bacteriophages infect bacteria only; they do not infect human cells (host range is set by bacterial surface receptors)

origin: Topic chosen from Kurzgesagt's most-viewed list (bacteriophage video, ~35M views) as a topic-pull experiment vs #0006. Script, structure, visuals and audio are original; their video was not downloaded, cut or referenced frame-by-frame (rule Q6).
